summary.headline: FY26 revenue rose 42.5% to INR84.22 crores, but EBITDA margin fell to 17% and PAT margin to 10.9% as spending on talent, platform and new verticals rose.
summary.overview: Chatterbox Technologies held its maiden earnings call for FY26 (year ended 31 March 2026), its first since its IPO. Revenue from operations grew 42.5% YoY to INR84.22 crores, and EBITDA and PAT rose in absolute terms to INR14.32 crores and INR9.2 crores. Margins moderated, which management attributed to investment in talent, platform capabilities and new verticals. Management declined to give formal guidance, though it said FY27 net margins would be similar to FY26 with an aim to expand them. Several questions focused on the sharp fall in market cap after listing, the possibility of a QYOU Media merger, the delayed results timeline, and the AAGE edutainment app; management answered most of these qualitatively or deferred them.

segments.name: Chatterbox Represent (exclusive talent management)
segments.commentary: Contributed 39.27% of FY26 revenue, the largest vertical. Management said margins are fixed but absolute contribution can grow as exclusive creators are added; it manages over 100 creators exclusively.

segments.name: Brand Solutions
segments.commentary: Contributed 36.18% of FY26 revenue. No separate growth or margin commentary was given in the call.

segments.name: ChtrSocial
segments.commentary: Contributed 24.55% of FY26 revenue. Management called it one of the fastest-growing verticals and among the highest-margin, and said it expects revenue to at least double in the coming period, without giving a percentage target.

segments.name: International (Chtr International / Dubai subsidiary)
segments.commentary: About 18% of FY26 revenue. Dubai subsidiary is the gateway to the Middle East; priority markets are MENA, with APAC and LATAM evaluated selectively. Management said it will expand in a lean way.

guidance_outlook: No formal financial guidance given. Management said the opportunity ahead is significantly larger and it remains optimistic on healthy medium- to long-term growth.
FY27 net margin expected to be similar to FY26 (about 10%); management said it is aiming higher and streamlining opex.
ChtrSocial expected to at least double its revenue in the upcoming period; no percentage target given.
AAGE edutainment app launch targeted within FY27 after development was paused for the IPO; it is still at the UX/UI stage with focus-group validation planned.
Management said integrated benefits from QYOU Media collaboration will become more visible in H2 2026.
capex_capacity: Intangible assets roughly doubled, while intangible assets under development stayed at INR4.68 crores; the AAGE app was on hold during the IPO and is being resumed.
Chtr Studios (video production) and Dubai subsidiary were established; the Dubai subsidiary is not 100% owned by Chatterbox (reason asked but not clearly answered in the call).
No capacity, utilisation or capex figures were disclosed.
demand_pricing: Management said growth came from a mix of higher ticket sizes, organic growth across verticals, new client wins and international expansion, with an equal-mix view endorsed by the analyst.
Over 500 brands served, more than 2,000 campaigns executed, and a team of over 100 professionals, per management.
Management does not disclose net revenue retention, but said a significant part of growth came from existing enterprise clients with larger mandates and cross-selling of ChtrSocial and Studios.
Creator economy said to grow at a 25-30% CAGR globally, and BCG estimate cited of over USD 1 trillion annual creator-economy spend by 2030.

qa_highlights.question: Which verticals will drive growth over the next 2-3 years, and will ChtrSocial, Represent, international or technology lead?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth will come from multiple engines: ChtrSocial, technology/AI platform, exclusive talent management and international (MENA first, then APAC and LATAM). No percentage targets were given.

qa_highlights.question: Which segments have the highest margins and where is operating leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Farrel Arora said ChtrSocial and the production arm (Studios) have the highest margin contribution. Represent is scalable in absolute rupee terms but its margins are fixed.

qa_highlights.question: Why has intangible assets under development stayed flat at INR4.68 crores, and what is the AAGE app?
qa_highlights.answer: AAGE was put on hold during the IPO. It is an edutainment app mixing short-form video, learning and gamification with AI; launch is targeted within FY27 after UX/UI curation.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR26 crore trade receivables is not yet due?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR17.5 crores is within the standard 60-day credit period. Management said collections usually realise in 60-90 days (around 70-75 days on average), and most of the not-due amount should now be realised.

qa_highlights.question: Did volume growth come from more campaigns, new clients or deeper wallet share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a mix of all three, with deeper wallet share from existing clients and international efforts contributing; no split was given.

qa_highlights.question: What are the reasons behind the Dubai subsidiary not being 100% owned, the top-five customers, and whether QYOU Media will merge with Chatterbox at a market cap of INR78 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Curt Marvis declined to comment on any merger, saying only that the company is always looking at ways to increase shareholder value and that a public vehicle enables accretive M&A. Top-five customer data and the Dubai ownership reason were not answered directly in the call.

risks_watch: Margin compression: EBITDA margin 17% and PAT margin 10.9% in FY26, with FY27 PAT margin guided at similar levels (about 10%). Watch whether opex is streamlined.
Receivables: INR26 crores of trade receivables at March 2026 against INR84.22 crores revenue. Track receivable days and cash conversion next quarter.
Results disclosure timing: results were announced on 29 May, with the investor presentation and call later, and a family matter was cited as the cause. Investor-relations sentiment was questioned.

Related-party and governance questions: the parent QYOU Media (listed in Canada/US) merger was raised but not addressed; the Dubai subsidiary ownership and the market-cap decline post-listing (analyst cited about INR78 crores vs about INR160 crores at debut) remain open.
Customer concentration: top-five customer contribution was asked for but not disclosed.
AAGE app launch in FY27 and its monetisation are unproven; management said it will validate the model first.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on long-term strategy and the creator-economy opportunity, but evasive on specifics: no formal guidance, no retention or net revenue retention metrics, no customer concentration data, and declined to comment on the QYOU merger question and on the investor-communication criticism.
key_quotes: FY26 numbers and the entire year was, let's call it a year of strategic investment, and all those investments are intended to drive sustainable value as we move forward.
Yes, that's not something that I would either comment on or discuss other than the fact that we're always looking at ways to increase shareholder value.
